# The Flutter target

What each PlainUI construct becomes, and what the generated file looks like.

The generated code is meant to be boring: no helper layer, no `_PuiWidgetBuilder`, no reflection.
If you deleted the compiler you could finish the file by hand.

## File shape

```dart
// GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT.
//
// Generated by PlainUI 1.0.0 from lib/ui/counter.pui.
// Target: Flutter 3.10+ / Dart 3. No deprecated APIs are emitted.
// Any change made here is overwritten the next time `plainui build` runs.
// Edit the .pui source instead.
//
// ignore_for_file: type=lint, unused_import

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// screen Counter — lib/ui/counter.pui:8
class Counter extends StatefulWidget { … }
```

- **Banner** names the source file, the compiler version and the Flutter generation the file
  targets, and disables two lint families that would
  otherwise fire on generated (not written-by-hand) code.
- **Imports** are grouped (dart → flutter → package → relative), sorted, de-duplicated, and
  re-based from the source directory to the output directory. Relative `.pui` imports become
  imports of the generated Dart file.
- **Comments** carry the declaration's kind and its source position, so a stack trace or a
  "go to definition" lands somewhere meaningful.

## Declarations

| PlainUI | Dart |
| --- | --- |
| `screen Home:` with no state | `class Home extends StatelessWidget` |
| `screen Home:` with `state` or a `task` | `StatefulWidget` + `_HomeState` |
| `component Card(title: String, children: List<Widget>):` | `StatelessWidget` with `final` fields and a `const` constructor |
| `component …` with `state` | `StatefulWidget` |
| `style price:` | `const TextStyle _puiStyle<Name>`, emitted only when referenced |
| `import "x.dart"` | `import 'x.dart';` |

Component constructors use named parameters (`{super.key, required this.title, …}`), and call
sites take named arguments too: positional arguments at the call site are mapped onto the
declared parameter names, so `Card("hi")` and `Card(title: "hi")` emit the same thing.

## Elements

| PlainUI | Flutter |
| --- | --- |
| `column`, `row` | `Column` / `Row`, with `gap=` expanded into `SizedBox` children |
| `stack` | `Stack` + `alignment` / `fit` |
| `wrap` | `Wrap` + `spacing` / `runSpacing` |
| `scroll` | `SingleChildScrollView(scrollDirection: …)` |
| `list` | `ListView(children: …)` |
| `grid` | `GridView.count(crossAxisCount: …)` |
| `card` | `Card` + `RoundedRectangleBorder` |
| `scaffold` | `Scaffold` + `AppBar(title: Text(…))` |
| `center` | `Center` |
| `align` | `Align(alignment: …)` |
| `expanded` | `Expanded(flex: …)` |
| `safeArea` | `SafeArea` |
| `spacer` | `Spacer(flex: …)` |
| `text` | `Text(…)`, converting non-strings (`count.toString()`, `items.join(', ')`) |
| `image` | `Image.network` / `Image.asset` (chosen from the literal source text) |
| `icon` | `Icon(Icons.<name>, size:, color:)` |
| `button` | `ElevatedButton` / `OutlinedButton` / `TextButton` from `variant` |
| `input` | `TextField` with controller, `obscureText`, `keyboardType`, `maxLines`, `autofocus` |
| `checkbox`, `toggle` | `CheckboxListTile` / `SwitchListTile` bound to state |
| `slider` | `Slider` bound to state |
| `divider` | `Divider` |
| `progress` | `LinearProgressIndicator` / `CircularProgressIndicator` |
| `Name(…)` (component) | `Name(named: args, children: <Widget>[…])` |
| `Name(…)` (not a component) | `Name(…)` verbatim, with an `info` diagnostic (`PUI2406`) |

## Universal properties

Every element accepts the same decoration properties, implemented by wrapping — which is why
they also work on component call sites:

| Property | Emitted wrapper |
| --- | --- |
| `padding` | `Padding` |
| `width`, `height`, `size` | `SizedBox` |
| `background`, `radius`, `border`, `borderColor`, `margin` | `Container` (+ `BoxDecoration`) |
| `opacity` | `Opacity` |
| `expand` | `Expanded` |
| `flex` (without `expand`) | `Flexible` |
| `align` | `Align` |

The wrappers are applied in a fixed order. Read from the element outwards:

```
element → Padding → SizedBox → Container (background, radius, border, margin)
        → Opacity → Expanded / Flexible → Align → gestures
```

So padding is closest to the element, sizing wraps the padded element, decoration wraps the
sized box, and layout is outermost — with the gesture detectors outside everything. The order is
pinned by `tests/codegen.test.ts` so it cannot drift silently.

`gap` is not a wrapper: it is expanded into `SizedBox` children between siblings, which is what
`mainAxisAlignment` cannot express.

## Gestures

`on tap:` on an element that handles taps natively (`button`, `checkbox`, …) becomes the
widget's own callback. On anything else, the generator adds a `GestureDetector` (tap, long press,
double tap) and/or a `MouseRegion` (hover), and a `Focus` widget for `focus` / `blur`:

```dart
Focus(
  onFocusChange: (hasFocus) {
    if (hasFocus) { … } else { … }
  },
  child: …,
)
```

## Actions

| PlainUI | Dart |
| --- | --- |
| `set count = count + 1` | inside one `setState(() { … })` for the whole run |
| consecutive `set`s | a single `setState` |
| `tasks.add(draft)` (state receiver) | inside `setState`, because it mutates state |
| `log("x")`, `save()` (host) | plain statement — wrapping would hide the side effect |
| `await save()` | the closure becomes `() async { … }` |
| `set x = await load()` | `final puiValueN = await load();` then `setState` — Dart forbids `await` in `setState` |
| `if cond:` inside a handler | `if (… ) { … } else { … }` |
| `navigate Detail(id: x)` | `Navigator.push(context, MaterialPageRoute<void>(builder: (_) => Detail(id: x)))` |
| `back()` | `Navigator.maybePop(context)` |

## Navigation

`navigate` is lowered to a real push of the target screen's own constructor. There is no route
name, no string lookup and no registry to keep in sync, so the arguments are checked by the Dart
compiler exactly as the `.pui` checker checked them:

```dart
ElevatedButton(
  onPressed: () {
    Navigator.push(
      context,
      MaterialPageRoute<void>(
        builder: (_) => Detail(id: "${index}", title: item),
      ),
    );
  },
  child: Text("Open"),
);
```

`back()` becomes `Navigator.maybePop(context)`: a pop that is safe on the first screen, so a screen
that is also the app's entry point needs no `canPop()` guard of its own.

A screen with parameters gets them as constructor arguments and fields, and its `State` reads them
through `widget.` — the same rule components follow:

```dart
class Detail extends StatelessWidget {
  const Detail({super.key, required this.id, this.title = "Task"});

  final String id;
  final String title;
  …
}
```

`context` is in scope wherever a handler is emitted (a `build` method's parameter, or a `State`'s
own `context`), which is why navigation is a statement and not an expression: there is no handler
in a value position to give it a `Navigator`.

### The route table

When a project navigates, one more file is generated beside the per-file output:

```dart
final Map<String, Widget Function(Map<String, Object?>)> puiRoutes = <String, Widget Function(Map<String, Object?>)>{
  'Detail': (args) => Detail(id: args['id']! as String, title: args['title'] as String? ?? "Task"),
  'Home': (args) => const Home(),
};
```

It exists for names that arrive from outside the source — a deep link, a push notification, a menu
built in Dart — where there is no import to the screen being opened. A project that declares no
parameters and never navigates gets no such file, which keeps generated directories as small as the
features they use.

Two rules keep the factories honest: a parameter with a **literal** default is passed only when the
caller supplied it (so opening by name and opening with `navigate` produce the same widget), and a
parameter whose default is not a literal is left to the constructor, with a comment saying so,
rather than being cast from a map that may not contain it.

## State and controllers

```dart
class _CounterState extends State<Counter> {
  int count = 0;
  String note = "";
  late final TextEditingController _noteController = TextEditingController(text: note);

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _noteController.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _syncControllers() {
    if (_noteController.text != note) {
      _noteController.text = note;
    }
  }
```

`bind=` creates one controller per bound state variable, a `dispose` override, and
`_syncControllers()` at the top of `build`. Controllers are declared `late final` so the
initializer can read the state field without ordering games. Everything else about state is
plain Dart fields and `setState`.

## Tasks

One `task` declaration becomes three fields, an `initState` call, and a loader:

```dart
class _TasksState extends State<Tasks> {
  List<String>? _items;
  String? _itemsError;
  bool _itemsLoading = true;
  int _itemsRequest = 0;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _loadItems();
  }

  Future<void> _loadItems() async {
    final request = ++_itemsRequest;
    setState(() {
      _itemsLoading = true;
      _itemsError = null;
    });
    try {
      final result = await loadItems();
      if (!mounted || request != _itemsRequest) return;
      setState(() {
        _items = result;
        _itemsLoading = false;
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (!mounted || request != _itemsRequest) return;
      setState(() {
        _itemsError = error.toString();
        _itemsLoading = false;
      });
    }
  }
}
```

`items.loading`, `items.error`, `items.value` and `items.retry()` are the only four expressions that
become these fields; anything else on a task is a compile error (`PUI2312`). A list-valued task reads
as `(_items ?? const <String>[])`, so a `for` over `items.value` runs before the first load completes
instead of throwing, and `items.error` inside `text` is emitted as `(_itemsError ?? '')` because
`Text` does not take a nullable string.

Three details are deliberate rather than incidental:

* `if (!mounted || request != _itemsRequest) return;` after the `await` — a screen can be popped
  while a load is in flight (`setState` on a disposed `State` throws), and a retry can start while an
  older load is still running. The older load finishes later, and without the sequence number its
  result would overwrite the newer one: the user retries a slow request and ends up looking at the
  stale answer, intermittently. `examples/async` contains exactly that race, and
  `flutter-verify.yml` asserts the fresh result survives it;
* the counter is per task, so two tasks in one screen can be in flight without interfering;
* the flag and the error are reset *before* the await, so a retry shows a spinner rather than the
  previous failure.

## Design tokens

A `theme` block compiles to data, and every use site is inlined:

```dart
theme App:
    color brand = #2563eb
    space md = 16
```

```dart
abstract final class AppTokens {
  /// `color brand`
  static const Color brand = Color(0xFF2563EB);
  /// `space md`
  static const double md = 16;
}
```

* `padding=md` becomes `const EdgeInsets.all(16)`, not `AppTokens.md`. Inlining is what keeps the
  generated trees `const` and makes the same `.pui` source produce the same numbers in every
  target; the tokens class exists so host Dart can reach the palette without copying hex strings.
* A theme that declares colour tokens also emits `AppTheme.light`: a `ThemeData` that fills the
  `ColorScheme` roles it can recognise by token name — `brand`/`primary`, `surface`/`background`,
  `ink`/`text`, `danger`/`error`, and otherwise a `seedColor` from the first colour — so Flutter's
  own widgets (buttons, text fields, the app bar) follow the design instead of Material's defaults.
* Tokens are compile-time values: assigning to one is `PUI2114`, using a colour token where a number
  belongs is `PUI2304`, and the checker (`PUI2305`–`PUI2309`) catches duplicate and shadowed names
  before Dart sees them.

## Text styles

`text "x" style=heading` becomes a Material theme lookup, so themes keep working:

```dart
Text("x", style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.headlineSmall)
```

`style=` combined with per-use properties produces `copyWith`:

```dart
Text("Total", style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodyMedium?.copyWith(fontWeight: FontWeight.w700))
```

Declared styles are private constants, emitted only when referenced (an unused private constant
is an `unused_element` lint error):

```dart
const TextStyle _puiStylePrice = TextStyle(fontSize: 20, fontWeight: FontWeight.w700, color: Color(0xFF1D4ED8));
```

## Conditionals, loops and slots

```plainui
if cart > 0:
    text "In cart: ${cart}"
else:
    text "Nothing yet"

for index, product in products:
    text product
```

```dart
if (cart > 0)
  Text("In cart: ${cart}")
else
  Text("Nothing yet"),

for (final (index, product) in products.indexed)
  Text(product),
```

Collection `if`/`for` inside the `children` list, so no builder widgets and no intermediate
lists. `slot` becomes `...children`.

## What the generator refuses to do

- **Generate with errors present.** No errors, no file. Half a widget tree is worse than none.
- **Invent types.** Unparseable annotations are passed through as written; `Int` is caught
  (`PUI2206`) because Dart would reject it, but `AppUser` is not second-guessed.
- **Format the output like prose.** Line breaks follow a simple rule — a call that fits stays on
  one line, otherwise one argument per line with a trailing comma — so diffs stay small.
- **Escape into the source map.** Comments mention `lib/ui/x.pui:12`; there are no
  `// ignore` tricks or generated identifiers beyond `_puiStyleX`, `puiValueN` and
  `_xController`.
